content:
The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears basketball team** represented **Missouri State University** during the **2014–15 NCAA Division I women's basketball season**. The Lady Bears, led by **head coach Kellie Harper** (in her 6th and final season before leaving for North Carolina State), competed in the **Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)** and played their home games at **JQH Arena** in Springfield, Missouri.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the team’s season:

---

### **Key Team Information**
- **Head Coach:** Kellie Harper (6th season)
- **Assistant Coaches:** Jackie Stiles, Jory Collins, Tisha Hill
- **Home Arena:** JQH Arena (Capacity: 11,000)
- **Conference:** Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)
- **Record:** **22–11 (13–5 MVC, 3rd place)**
- **Postseason:** **WNIT (Women’s National Invitation Tournament) – Second Round**

---

### **Roster & Key Players**
The 2014–15 team featured a mix of experienced upperclassmen and talented newcomers. Some of the standout players included:

| **Player**            | **Position** | **Year** | **Key Stats (2014–15)** |
|-----------------------|-------------|----------|-------------------------|
| **Alexis Prince**     | G/F         | Senior   | 14.2 PPG, 6.1 RPG, 2.1 APG |
| **Tyler Cook**        | F           | Junior   | 12.3 PPG, 6.8 RPG, 1.5 BPG |
| **Lacy Ellis**        | C           | Senior   | 8.1 PPG, 5.4 RPG, 1.2 BPG |
| **Hannah Wilkerson**  | G           | Sophomore| 9.8 PPG, 3.2 RPG, 2.1 APG |
| **Camille Redmon**    | G           | Freshman | 6.5 PPG, 2.8 RPG, 1.5 APG |
| **Megan Pearson**     | G           | Junior   | 5.2 PPG, 2.1 APG |
| **Whitney Edens**     | G           | Senior   | 4.7 PPG, 1.8 RPG |

- **Alexis Prince** was the team’s leading scorer and a **First-Team All-MVC** selection.
- **Tyler Cook** was a dominant post presence and earned **Second-Team All-MVC** honors.
- **Lacy Ellis** provided veteran leadership in the paint.
- **Hannah Wilkerson** emerged as a key sophomore guard.

---

### **Season Highlights & Notable Games**
#### **Non-Conference Play (7–6)**
- The Lady Bears struggled early, going **4–6** in their first 10 games, including losses to **#11 Texas A&M (L 53–72)**, **Arkansas (L 58–63)**, and **Oral Roberts (L 59–63)**.
- They finished non-conference play with a **7–6** record, including a **6-game winning streak** to close out December.

#### **Missouri Valley Conference Play (13–5, 3rd Place)**
- Missouri State was **picked to finish 3rd in the MVC preseason poll** behind **Wichita State and Drake**.
- **Key MVC Wins:**
  - **Swept Wichita State** (71–63 at home, 68–65 on the road)
  - **Split with Drake** (W 76–69 at home, L 62–75 on the road)
  - **Swept Illinois State** (78–65, 71–63)
  - **Beat Northern Iowa twice** (68–58, 72–65)
- **Key MVC Losses:**
  - **Lost to Drake** (62–75) in a crucial late-season game.
  - **Split with Southern Illinois** (W 73–61, L 62–68).
- The Lady Bears finished **3rd in the MVC** with a **13–5** record, behind **Drake (16–2)** and **Wichita State (14–4)**.

#### **MVC Tournament (Semifinal Loss)**
- **Quarterfinal:** Defeated **Evansville 78–58**
- **Semifinal:** Lost to **Drake 55–68** (ending their tournament run)

---

### **Postseason: WNIT (Women’s National Invitation Tournament)**
- Missouri State received an **at-large bid** to the **2015 WNIT** (their first WNIT appearance since 2011).
- **First Round:** Defeated **Arkansas State 68–56** (March 19, 2015)
- **Second Round:** Lost to **Iowa 56–69** (March 23, 2015) – **Season ends at 22–11**

---

### **Awards & Honors**
- **Alexis Prince** – **First-Team All-MVC**, MVC All-Tournament Team
- **Tyler Cook** – **Second-Team All-MVC**
- **Kellie Harper** – **MVC Coach of the Year** (her 3rd MVC COY award)
- **Hannah Wilkerson** – MVC All-Freshman Team (2013–14, but contributed significantly in 2014–15)

---

### **Coaching Change & Legacy**
- **Kellie Harper left after the season** to become the head coach at **North Carolina State** (her alma mater).
- She was replaced by **Amaka Agugua-Hamilton** (who later led the program to greater success, including NCAA Tournament appearances).
- The **2014–15 team** was a **transition year**, setting the stage for future success under Agugua-Hamilton.
- **Jackie Stiles** (former WNBA star and Missouri State legend) was an assistant coach this season before later becoming interim head coach in 2021.

---

### **Statistical Leaders (2014–15)**
| **Category**       | **Player**         | **Stat** |
|--------------------|--------------------|----------|
| **Points**         | Alexis Prince      | 14.2 PPG |
| **Rebounds**       | Tyler Cook         | 6.8 RPG  |
| **Assists**        | Hannah Wilkerson   | 2.1 APG  |
| **Steals**         | Alexis Prince      | 1.5 SPG  |
| **Blocks**         | Tyler Cook         | 1.5 BPG  |
| **Field Goal %**   | Lacy Ellis         | 52.4%    |
| **Three-Point %**  | Whitney Edens      | 37.5%    |
| **Free Throw %**   | Alexis Prince      | 80.2%    |

---

### **Season Summary & Impact**
- **22–11 record** was the **best since 2010–11** (26–7, NCAA Tournament).
- **First WNIT appearance since 2011** (ended in the 2nd round).
- **Strong MVC finish (3rd place)** despite early struggles.
- **Alexis Prince** had a **breakout senior season**, becoming one of the best players in the MVC.
- **Kellie Harper’s final season** before her move to NC State—she left the program in good shape for her successor.
- The team’s **defensive improvement** (holding opponents to **60.1 PPG**) was a key factor in their success.

---

### **Where Are They Now?**
- **Alexis Prince** – Played professionally overseas (Spain, Australia, Israel) before becoming a coach (currently an assistant at **Texas Tech**).
- **Tyler Cook** – Played professionally in Europe (Portugal, Sweden).
- **Hannah Wilkerson** – Transferred to **Arkansas State** after the 2015–16 season.
- **Kellie Harper** – Later became head coach at **Tennessee (2019–present)**.
- **Jackie Stiles** – Became Missouri State’s **interim head coach in 2021** before leaving for **Oregon State**.

---

### **Final Thoughts**
The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears** were a **resilient team** that overcame early struggles to post a **22-win season** and make the **WNIT**. While they fell short of an NCAA Tournament bid, they laid the groundwork for future success under **Amaka Agugua-Hamilton**. **Alexis Prince’s leadership** and **Kellie Harper’s final season** were highlights, making this a memorable year in program history.
